title: Config, .gitignore, .gitattributes, and Hooks
intro: The settings around a repository decide whether secrets get committed, whether Windows and Linux users fight over line endings, and whether checks run before a commit. Most of it is set once and forgotten, so it pays to set it deliberately.

steps.prompt: Show every Git setting in effect, and which file each one comes from.
steps.fake_output:
file:/etc/gitconfig                 core.autocrlf=input
file:/home/alice/.gitconfig         user.name=Alice
file:/home/alice/.gitconfig         pull.rebase=true
file:.git/config                    user.email=alice@acme.example
file:.git/config                    remote.origin.url=git@github.com:acme/shop.git
steps.explanation: Three levels: system, global (your user), and this repository, which overrides the others.
steps.why: When Git behaves differently on two machines, this shows why. The per-repo level is how you use a work email in work repos and a personal one elsewhere ('includeIf' in ~/.gitconfig automates that by directory).

steps.prompt: A file build/output.log isn't showing up as untracked. Find out which ignore rule is hiding it.
steps.explanation: Line 14 of .gitignore ignores the whole build/ directory.
steps.why: check-ignore -v names the exact file, line, and pattern responsible, which beats reading several ignore files (.gitignore in any directory, .git/info/exclude, and your global excludes file) and guessing.

steps.prompt: config/secrets.yml was committed long ago and is now in .gitignore, but Git still tracks it. Stop tracking it while keeping the file on disk.
steps.explanation: The file is removed from the index (staged as a deletion) but still exists locally.
steps.why: .gitignore only affects untracked files; anything already committed stays tracked. Remember that this doesn't remove the secret from history: every old commit still has it, so rotate it (security-tutorial-009).

steps.prompt: The team added a .gitattributes with '* text=auto' to settle line endings. Re-apply it to every tracked file so the fix is one clean commit.
steps.fake_output: (no output: files whose line endings changed are staged)
steps.explanation: Files are re-normalised to LF in the repository and staged.
steps.why: .gitattributes is committed, so it applies to everyone, unlike core.autocrlf, which is a per-machine setting that people have set differently. '* text=auto' stores LF in the repo and lets each OS check out its own ending. git-incident-005 is what happens without it.

steps.prompt: Share hooks with the team: tell Git to run hooks from the committed directory .githooks instead of .git/hooks.
steps.fake_output: (no output: hooks are now read from .githooks)
steps.explanation: A pre-commit script in .githooks/ now runs for you before each commit.
steps.why: .git/hooks isn't versioned, so hooks there never reach teammates. core.hooksPath (or a tool like pre-commit or husky) makes them part of the repo. Hooks are a convenience, not a control: anyone can skip them with --no-verify, so the same checks must also run in CI.

steps.fake_output: (no output: 'git lg' now works in every repository)
steps.explanation: 'git lg' runs the long log command.
steps.why: Aliases live in your global config, so they follow you everywhere. Keep them for commands you run all day; an alias you have to look up saves nothing.
